transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-23
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Samir (SE), Lena (CSM) -- Dana, Mark, Priya, Carlos (Bluecrest)
---
Summary:
Short: Renewal discussion + regional expansion (EU + APAC), proposal to add dedicated capacity burst for BlackFriday-style release; require security review for EU data residency and VPC setup. Agreed to run a performance benchmark and draft amendment for pricing.
Topics covered:
- Current usage and forecast for next 12 months
- Latency envelope and SLOs for EU customers
- Dedicated capacity vs hosted burst economics
- VPC/on-prem options and KMS/SSO considerations
- Next steps: benchmark, amendment, onboarding checklist
---
[00:00] Ava Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off. we wanted to review your renewal, and the expansion ask into eu and apac, plus the burst capacity for q4. is that still right dana?
[00:22] Dana Liu: yea thanks ava, yeah the quarter is coming up. quick context, we're doing a phased rollout — us, then eu then apac. main ask is keep latency under 220ms P95 for EU production and also have a burst floor for marketing spikes.
[00:40] Mark Roberts: and from our side we saw token growth 2.5x qtr over qtr, so cost is a big part of the talk, we want to avoid doubling spend.
[00:56] Samir Patel: quick question on "burst floor" — are you thinking reserved dedicated nodes or just higher hosted quotas? those are different tradeoffs.
[01:12] Priya Shah: ideally dedicated for the eu region because of data residency plus predictable tail latency, but we also want a cheaper hosted fallback for non-critical traffic.
[01:29] Ava Martinez: right, so what we've seen work for other customers is a hybrid: dedicated capacity for core traffic + hosted overflow. we can show an amendment with both tiered pricing and automatic fallback.
[01:45] Carlos Mendes: procurement question — will the amendment change invoicing? we prefer one invoice but can accept a line-item for dedicated reserve. also need net 60 terms discussed.
[02:03] Ava Martinez: noted, i'll include invoicing options. we'll propose monthly invoice with an annual commitment discount applied, and a separate one-off for onboarding if you want.
[02:18] Dana Liu: on security, EU data at rest must stay in region and we need SOC2 type 2 docs and a KMS integration. any blockers there?
[02:31] Samir Patel: we support KMS integrations for private deployments and VPC peering for Dedicated — for hosted we do configurable residency, but if you need customer-managed keys that's generally part of Private mode.
[02:47] Mark Roberts: hmm we want customer-managed keys for EU. that pushes us toward Private or Dedicated + bring-your-own-key?
[02:58] Lena Ko: to clarify, dedicated pools can be configured with regional lock and we can support KMS through our enterprise offering, but true BYOK with HSM-backed KMS is generally Private. i'll follow up with the exact matrix.
[03:18] Priya Shah: okay that helps. also can we get a read on expected cold-start latencies? our sequences average 600 tokens.
[03:28] Samir Patel: sequence length 600 tokens, that changes kernel selection and batching. for Dedicated we can tune kernels and batching to keep P95 down — for hosted it'll vary but we can run a 24-hr sim.
[03:45] Mark Roberts: the sim is key — we need to see dedicated vs hosted numbers for both latency and tokens/sec costing at our prompt mix.
[03:55] Ava Martinez: agreed. samir will run a benchmark using your sample prompts. we'll do two runs: hosted baseline and dedicated profile on a GPU type that's comparable.
[04:08] Dana Liu: timeline? we need results before next week so we can finalize numbers with finance.
[04:15] Samir Patel: i can run a 1-day focused benchmark and aim to share results by monday the 30th (i'll double check resource allocation).
[04:26] Carlos Mendes: monday works for commercial review. procurement also asked for a copy of SOC2 and ISO certs, and the DPA.
[04:36] Ava Martinez: i'll attach security pack. lena will include the DPA and RBAC guide.
[04:44] Lena Ko: yes i'll drop the onboarding checklist and the RBAC template, plus a quick howto for SSO/SAML mapping.
[04:54] Mark Roberts: question on automatic fallback — if dedicated is saturated will the tokens route to hosted? does that affect logs/audit and costs?
[05:06] Samir Patel: good point — the routing preserves request metadata and we annotate which model variant served the request in the logs. cost will show up on the hosted line item, but we can add a cap and alerting so you don't unexpectedly burn.
[05:23] Priya Shah: can we enforce region-only fallback? i.e., if eu dedicated full, fallback still within eu hosted region?
[05:33] Samir Patel: yes we can set routing policy by region. the only caveat is capacity — if eu-hosted is exhausted, cross-region failover can be enabled or disabled per policy.
[05:45] Dana Liu: regarding canary and rollouts — we're going to do a canary for the new model in staging before q4 launch. will Redwood support canary percent rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions?
[06:00] Ava Martinez: yes, we have built-in rollout controls and quality monitoring; we can tie alerts to your eval sets and automatically rollback if hit regression thresholds.
[06:12] Mark Roberts: good. also, pricing question — do you have volume tiers for embeddings vs generation? our mix is ~70% gen tokens, 30% embeddings for similarity search.
[06:25] Ava Martinez: we can show blended pricing and a breakout for embeddings. the amendment will include a blended per-token price for generation and per-embedding unit price.
[06:38] Carlos Mendes: what's the delta for dedicated reserved capacity? ballpark percent?
[06:44] Ava Martinez: typically 18-28% discount vs on-demand hosted unit cost depending on commit length and GPU family. i'll put a conservative 20% in the draft.
[06:56] Priya Shah: we also need SLA language for P95 latency in eu and credits if we miss. is that part of the enterprise package?
[07:06] Ava Martinez: enterprise SLA can include latency SLOs with defined credit formulas. legal will need to review but we can propose SLO targets and compensation model.
[07:18] Dana Liu: acceptance criteria for the renewal: 1) amendment with region pricing, 2) successful benchmark showing P95 < 220ms on Dedicated for our sample, 3) SOC2 + DPA in docs, 4) onboarding checklist and timeline.
[07:34] Lena Ko: noted. i'll map those into the onboarding playbook and include a timeline for EU activation (~3 weeks prep once PO issued).
[07:45] Mark Roberts: any network peering windows? our infra team prefers BGP peering and will want to schedule maintenance windows.
[07:54] Samir Patel: we support VPC peering and private link; maintenance windows can be negotiated. for private deployments we do direct connect style peering.
[08:07] Priya Shah: one small transcription note, in logs we saw some "KV cache" mentions — can you describe how prefix/KV caching will behave across region failover?
[08:18] Samir Patel: prefix cache is local to the serving pool; if you failover across region you'll miss cached KV and that could add cold token cost on first request. we do warmup strategies and prefetch to mitigate.
[08:33] Dana Liu: okay good to know. back to a commercial ask — if we add apac later can we stage pricing so the uplift for APAC is lighter if we commit now?
[08:44] Ava Martinez: yes we can structure the amendment with future region add-ons at fixed uplift percentages so you lock in price for later activation.
[08:55] Carlos Mendes: perfect. on the legal side, any change to the DPA for regional residency?
[09:02] Lena Ko: minor addendum to DPA to add regional processing terms; we can provide standard language.
[09:10] Mark Roberts: before we wrap, do you have a sample runbook for incident triage? we want 24/7 support in q4.
[09:18] Ava Martinez: enterprise support offering includes 24/7 for Sev1 with an escalation matrix; i'll include a runbook sample in the pack.
[09:28] Dana Liu: great. can you put tentative dates: PO by sept 6, eu activation week sept 20, q4 ramp ready by oct 15?
[09:40] Ava Martinez: noted, we'll aim for PO week of sept 6. we'll confirm benchmark results and amendment before then.
[09:50] Samir Patel: action: i'll kick off the benchmark with your prompt set. please attach sample prompts to the follow-up email.
[09:58] Priya Shah: will do.
